CHIEF COMPLAINT
Kidney screening in patient with Smith-Magenis Syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 3/7 week gestation twin, birthweight 4 pounds 8 ounces. She was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis Syndrome by a neurologist. As an infant, she experienced feeding difficulties with apnea during feeding and difficulty with temperature regulation. She has severe reflux managed by a GI doctor and was transitioned off cow's milk per dietician recommendation. She had developmental delay, not sitting or walking by one year of age, but is now crawling and attempting to take steps. She is currently enrolled in feeding therapy, occupational therapy, and physical therapy, with speech therapy to begin within the next couple of weeks. She has been evaluated by multiple specialists including allergist, orthopedic specialist, ophthalmologist, and audiology. The patient's twin sister is unaffected and doing well. During genetic evaluation, parents were informed that patients with Smith-Magenis Syndrome may develop kidney problems including possible kidney fusion. Current fluid intake includes pea protein milk, water, and occasional juice. Patient has 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Regular urination with 8-10 wet diapers per 24 hours. Adequate fluid intake.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis Syndrome. Prematurity (34 3/7 weeks gestation). Severe gastroesophageal reflux. Cow's milk intolerance. Developmental delay. Hypotonia.

MEDICATIONS
Not discussed.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother, age 9, with autism. Twin sister without apparent medical problems, approximately same size as patient.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives in Dallas, Georgia.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 3/7 week gestation twin with Smith-Magenis Syndrome, a chromosomal deletion syndrome affecting multiple organ systems. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in patients with this syndrome. Plan is to obtain renal ultrasound screening today. If abnormalities are identified, further management and follow-up will be determined. Follow-up care to be provided at town center location in Dallas.
